outcome: Proportion of women with sphincter function impairment identified by EAUS and AM
Impact of AM results on mode of birth counseling
cohort: 1348 women who underwent symptom assessment and anorectal studies using EAUS and AM after OASI
finding: Anal manometry (AM) identifies a higher proportion of women with sphincter function impairment compared to endoanal ultrasound (EAUS) alone, suggesting its importance in mode of birth counseling after obstetric anal sphincter injury.
mod_finding: Anal manometry (AM) alongside endoanal ultrasound helps identify more women with sphincter function impairment, enabling accurate mode of birth counseling and potentially impacting decisions regarding cesarean delivery.
